items.name: Product Start Plan
items.description: Follow one step at a time. Test the idea before you spend more.

variables.competitorFocus: price, product format, presentation and buyer complaints
variables.costFocus: materials, packaging, selling fees and delivery
variables.complianceFocus: applicable registrations, safety, labeling and claims
variables.supplierFocus: quality, minimum quantities, lead times and reliability
variables.packagingFocus: protect the product and communicate the offer clearly
variables.salesChannels: one direct channel and one local or marketplace channel
variables.scaleEvidence: repeatable quality, real paying customers and workable direct costs and results
variables.riskWarning: Do not commit to large inventory before testing.

steps.title: Check If Buyers Will Pay for {{productPlural}}
steps.description: Check whether {{customer}} care enough about {{product}} to pay a realistic price.

content.text: Opinions and compliments do not justify inventory. Look for proof from people who match the intended buyer and already spend on similar products or occasions.

checklist.label: Speak with at least {{validationTargetCount}} likely buyers
Ask what they buy today and what frustrates them
Record the price or clear action each person would consider

warnings: {{riskWarning}}
tips: Ask about a recent purchase before showing your concept.

options.label: Yes, proof is strong enough
options.description: Continue with focused market research while keeping the first test small.

options.label: Not yet
options.description: Narrow the buyer, occasion or offer and run more conversations before spending.

steps.nextBestAction: Speak with {{validationTargetCount}} likely buyers and record current buying behavior and readiness to pay.

steps.title: See What Buyers Use Today
steps.description: Review competing offers through the lens of {{competitorFocus}}.

content.text: Competitor research should reveal buyer expectations and gaps, not encourage copying. Use it to define a narrower and more credible test.

checklist.label: Review at least five relevant sellers or offers
Read buyer reviews and note repeated praise or complaints
Write one practical way {{product}} will be clearer or more useful

tips: Include local and online alternatives where both matter to the buyer.
steps.nextBestAction: Review five relevant offers and write down prices, presentation choices and repeated buyer complaints.

steps.title: Make a Small Test Batch
steps.description: Create the smallest batch that can test {{qualityFocus}} and buyer response.

content.text: The first test is for learning, not for filling a catalogue. Keep variations and quantities low enough that weak proof is inexpensive.

checklist.label: Document the production or sourcing process
Collect direct feedback from intended buyers

warnings: {{riskWarning}}
steps.nextBestAction: Complete the smallest useful test batch and record quality and buyer feedback.

steps.title: Check What Each Sale Really Costs
steps.description: List the obvious direct costs before setting a test price.

content.text: A sale is not useful proof if packaging, fees, delivery or waste make it structurally unworkable. Use the calculators below to keep the estimate explicit and revisable.

checklist.label: Estimate waste, failed units or sample cost
Calculate a per-unit or per-order estimate
Write down the ideas to test that still need verification

warnings: Do not treat your time or delivery effort as free.
steps.nextBestAction: Create a cost estimate covering {{costFocus}} and record ideas to test that still need proof.

steps.title: Check the Rules Before You Sell
steps.description: Verify {{complianceFocus}} using current official sources before commercial sale.

content.text: Requirements depend on the product, claims, location and sales channel. This plan cannot determine legal eligibility. save the official sources and complete applicable steps.

checklist.label: Identify the relevant regulator or official authority
Check labeling, disclosure and claim requirements
Save links to current official sources
Complete rules you need to follow before commercial sale

warnings: Do not rely only on marketplace listings, social posts or another seller's interpretation.
steps.nextBestAction: Identify the relevant authority and save current official guidance for {{productPlural}}.

steps.title: Compare Suppliers
steps.description: Compare suppliers for {{supplierFocus}} without committing to unnecessary stock.

content.text: A low quote is not useful if quality changes, minimum quantities are risky or replenishment is unreliable.

checklist.label: Identify at least three relevant suppliers
Request samples or the smallest practical quantity
Record a backup option for the most important input

tips: Keep written notes on specifications and what each quote includes.
steps.nextBestAction: Shortlist three suppliers and request samples or small-quantity terms.

steps.title: Make the Offer Easy to Understand
steps.description: Prepare packaging that can {{packagingFocus}} without consuming the test budget.

content.text: Early presentation should build trust and make the offer understandable. It does not need a large custom packaging order.

checklist.label: Choose a clear working name and product promise
Prepare simple packaging appropriate for the test
Create honest photos of the actual test product

warnings: Do not hide product limitations or use unsupported quality, health or performance claims.
steps.nextBestAction: Prepare one simple, compliant package and photograph the real product clearly.

steps.title: Set a Test Price
steps.description: Choose a price that reflects direct cost, buyer expectations and the purpose of the test.

content.text: Deep discounts can create false demand. Test whether intended buyers accept a price that has a plausible path to workable costs and results.

checklist.label: Compare the relevant market price range
Choose one test price and explain the value
Define the maximum discount or offer you will allow

warnings: Do not test demand using an unsustainable friends-and-family discount.
steps.nextBestAction: Set one test price and record why it is plausible for both the buyer and the business.

steps.title: Pick Your First Sales Channels
steps.description: Focus on {{salesChannels}} instead of opening every possible channel.

content.text: A narrow channel test makes it easier to understand where inquiries and paid orders actually come from.

checklist.label: Choose one primary channel where {{customer}} already pay attention
Choose at most one secondary test channel
Prepare one clear product message and call to action
Define how orders, delivery and questions will be handled

tips: Track conversations and paid orders manually. do not mistake reach for demand.
steps.nextBestAction: Publish the real test offer on the primary channel and contact likely buyers directly.

steps.title: Get Your First Paid Sales
steps.description: Work toward {{firstPaidMilestone}} and record what happened on every order.

content.text: Paid behavior reveals more than likes. Record price, channel, delivery effort, quality issues and whether the buyer would return or refer someone.

checklist.label: Record each paid order and sales channel
Record direct cost and delivery issues
Ask buyers what nearly stopped the purchase
Track repeat, referral or gifting interest

decisionGates.question: Have you reached {{firstPaidMilestone}} with credible real paying customers?

options.label: Yes, review the proof
options.description: Move to a structured review before increasing inventory.

options.label: Not yet
options.description: Return to the channel and offer test. do not call unpaid interest a sale.

steps.nextBestAction: Make the next direct sales attempt and keep the paid-order record current.

steps.title: Check Demand, Quality and Costs
steps.description: Decide whether the proof supports growing, another controlled test or a pause.

content.text: The review should use paid behavior, quality consistency and obvious direct costs and results. Stopping or changing a weak offer is a valid result.

checklist.label: Summarize real paying customers and the strongest sales channel
Review quality failures, returns and delivery effort
Review direct cost and accepted price
Write the strongest reason to continue and the strongest reason to stop

options.label: Grow by Repeating What Works
options.description: Run one measured growth experiment with a defined budget and stop condition.

options.label: Improve and retest
options.description: Change the offer, cost, price or channel before another small sales test.

options.label: Pause this idea
options.description: Record why the proof is weak. Do not invest more until a better hypothesis exists.

steps.nextBestAction: Review real paying customers, quality and direct costs and results and choose the proof-based path.

steps.title: Grow What Is Working
steps.description: Increase only one constraint at a time after {{finalDecisionMilestone}}.

content.text: More stock and more channels amplify unresolved quality, compliance and margin problems. grow only the part already supported by proof.

checklist.label: Set a maximum inventory or promotion budget
Define the result and stop condition
Keep a fallback supplier or delivery plan

warnings: Do not grow unresolved quality, compliance, delivery or direct-cost problems.
steps.nextBestAction: Write one measured growth experiment with a budget, success metric and stop condition.

items.name: Digital Product Start Plan
items.description: Follow one step at a time. Test the idea before you spend more.

variables.competitorFocus: use case, format, price, reviews and missing guidance
variables.usabilityFocus: whether users can reach the promised outcome without extra explanation
variables.rightsFocus: asset rights, license terms, delivery and refund expectations
variables.pricingFocus: buyer value, competing options and support effort
variables.salesChannels: one relevant marketplace or direct channel
variables.distributionFocus: the channel that produced qualified visits and paid buyers
variables.riskWarning: Do not build a large bundle before the smallest useful version is tested.
variables.validationCriteria: confirm the problem and show credible readiness to pay

steps.title: Pick One Customer to Help
steps.description: Confirm the importance of {{problem}} for {{customer}}.

content.text: A broad audience leads to a vague product. Start with recent behavior, current workarounds and a specific outcome the buyer already values.

checklist.label: Speak with at least {{validationTargetCount}} matching people
Ask what they use today and what it costs in time or effort
Record what clear action would count as real interest

warnings: {{riskWarning}}

decisionGates.question: Did {{validationTargetCount}} people you want to help {{validationCriteria}}?

options.label: Yes, the need is clear
options.description: Research current alternatives before defining the product.

options.label: Not yet
options.description: Narrow the buyer or problem and test again.

steps.nextBestAction: Interview {{validationTargetCount}} people you want to help about their current plan and desired outcome.

steps.title: See What Customers Use Today
steps.description: Review alternatives through {{competitorFocus}}.

content.text: Alternatives include free files, manual processes and general-purpose tools. Understand why buyers use them and where they still struggle.

checklist.label: Review at least five relevant alternatives
Read reviews or user discussions for repeated friction
Write one narrow gap worth testing

steps.nextBestAction: Review five alternatives and document the repeated gap your product will test.

steps.title: Pick the Smallest Useful Product
steps.description: Choose the minimum version of {{product}} that can deliver one clear outcome.

content.text: File count is not value. Remove features and extras that do not help the first buyer complete the promised task.

checklist.label: List the minimum files, pages or features needed
List what the first version will deliberately exclude
Define how a buyer will know the product worked

warnings: {{riskWarning}}
steps.nextBestAction: Write the one-sentence outcome and the minimum contents needed to deliver it.

steps.title: Build the Smallest Useful Version
steps.description: Build a usable first version in {{formatFocus}}.

content.text: The first version exists to test usefulness and usability, not to demonstrate every possible feature or style.

checklist.label: Use realistic examples or sample data
Write brief setup or use instructions
Test the delivered files or access flow

steps.nextBestAction: Build the smallest usable version and test the actual delivery format.

steps.title: Watch Real Users Try It
steps.description: Observe {{customer}} using the product without coaching.

content.text: A polished preview cannot compensate for confusing setup, unclear labels or a product that fails during real use.

checklist.label: Give the product to at least three people you want to help
Observe where users hesitate or make errors
Ask whether the outcome saved meaningful time or effort
Fix issues that block the core outcome

tips: Separate requests for decorative extras from problems that block usefulness.
steps.nextBestAction: Observe three people you want to help and fix the largest barrier to the promised outcome.

steps.title: Check Rights and Selling Rules
steps.description: Confirm {{rightsFocus}} before publishing.

content.text: Digital products can include fonts, images, code or source material with different usage rights. Buyers also need clear access and usage expectations.

checklist.label: Verify commercial rights for every included asset
Write a simple buyer license or usage boundary
Define delivery, updates and refund expectations
Test access with a clean buyer account or device

warnings: Do not resell assets, code or source material without the required rights.
steps.nextBestAction: Verify asset rights and write clear usage and delivery terms.

steps.title: Set a Test Price
steps.description: Choose a test price using {{pricingFocus}}.

content.text: Free downloads test interest in free material, not willingness to buy. The first price should be understandable and support the intended delivery effort.

checklist.label: Relate the price to the buyer outcome
Define what support or updates are included

steps.nextBestAction: Set one test price and state the outcome and support included.

steps.title: Choose Where to Sell It
steps.description: Publish first through {{salesChannels}}.

content.text: A strong listing shows the actual product, intended buyer and result. It should not rely on vague bundles or inflated file counts.

checklist.label: Create previews using the real product
Write the intended buyer, outcome and contents clearly
Add setup, compatibility and usage details

steps.nextBestAction: Create an honest preview and complete the listing on one primary channel.

steps.title: Share It With a Small Group
steps.description: Put the paid offer in front of people who match {{customer}}.

content.text: Qualified direct feedback is more useful than broad low-intent traffic. Start with a small audience you can observe and support.

checklist.label: Invite at least 10 likely customers or audience members
Record visits, meaningful inquiries and purchases

steps.nextBestAction: Share the paid offer with 10 likely customers and record what they do.

steps.title: Get Your First Paying Buyers
steps.description: Work toward {{firstPaidMilestone}} and support real use.

content.text: Paid buyers reveal whether the promise, preview, price and product work together. Record support effort as well as sales.

checklist.label: Record each paid sale and finding customers source
Ask buyers what made the offer credible
Record setup problems, refunds and support time
Ask whether the product delivered the promised outcome

decisionGates.question: Have you reached {{firstPaidMilestone}} with buyers who can use the product?

options.label: Yes, review the proof
options.description: Review usefulness, support effort and channel quality.

options.label: Not yet
options.description: Improve the listing, product usability or qualified distribution before expanding.

steps.nextBestAction: Reach the next paid buyer and record finding customers source and product outcome.

steps.title: Review What You Learned
steps.description: Use paid feedback and {{distributionFocus}} to choose whether to expand, improve or pause.

content.text: More products and channels create maintenance work. Expand only after the core product reliably delivers its outcome.

checklist.label: Summarize paid buyer outcomes and complaints
Identify the strongest finding customers source
Choose the one improvement most likely to help the core outcome

decisionGates.question: Does the paid proof support broader distribution?

options.label: Grow by Repeating What Works
options.description: Add one product variation or one qualified distribution channel.

options.label: Improve and retest
options.description: Fix the core usability, promise or listing before seeking more traffic.

options.label: Pause this product
options.description: Record why paid proof is weak and avoid producing a larger bundle.

steps.nextBestAction: Review paid feedback and choose expansion, one focused improvement or a pause.

steps.title: Grow What Is Working
steps.description: Expand only after {{finalDecisionMilestone}}.

content.text: The safest next move is one measured variation or channel, not a large catalogue built on untested ideas to test.

checklist.label: Choose one new variation, bundle or channel
Define the buyer and expected outcome
Set a time or promotion limit
Track paid sales and support effort

steps.nextBestAction: Choose one distribution experiment with a success metric and stop condition.

items.name: Service Start Plan
items.description: Follow one step at a time. Test the idea before you spend more.

variables.pricingFocus: scope, delivery effort, buyer value and revision boundaries
variables.outreachChannel: one channel where likely customers can be reached responsibly
variables.scalePath: a repeatable offer and delivery process
variables.riskWarning: Do not promise a broad result you cannot control or deliver consistently.
variables.validationCriteria: confirm the problem is important enough to address now

steps.title: Pick One Customer to Help
steps.description: Focus on {{customer}} and when {{problem}} becomes costly or urgent.

content.text: A narrow customer makes the offer, proof and outreach easier to evaluate. You can broaden later after a repeatable result exists.

checklist.label: Name the role most affected by {{problem}}
Identify the trigger that makes action timely
List where these possible customers can be reached responsibly

steps.nextBestAction: Write one customer segment, decision-maker and urgent trigger.

steps.title: Check If the Problem Is Real
steps.description: Confirm how {{customer}} currently handle {{problem}} and what it costs them.

content.text: Generic interest in a service is weak proof. Look for a current workaround, visible consequence and willingness to change.

checklist.label: Speak with at least {{validationTargetCount}} likely customers
Ask how the problem is handled today
Record time, risk, missed revenue or frustration without inventing numbers
Ask what result would justify action

warnings: {{riskWarning}}

options.label: Yes, define the offer
options.description: Package a narrow service around the confirmed outcome.

options.label: Not yet
options.description: Refine the customer or problem before building proof or doing broad outreach.

steps.nextBestAction: Interview {{validationTargetCount}} likely customers about their current process and desired result.

steps.title: Build the Smallest Useful Offer
steps.description: Package {{offer}} around a clear outcome, scope and boundary.

content.text: possible customers need to understand what changes, what is included and what remains their responsibility.

checklist.label: List deliverables and what is excluded
Define client inputs, access and decision responsibilities
Write the next step for a qualified prospect

steps.nextBestAction: Write a one-page offer with outcome, deliverables, exclusions and client responsibilities.

steps.title: Show Proof You Can Help
steps.description: Build {{proofAsset}} that demonstrates the approach without pretending to prove every result.

content.text: Relevant proof reduces perceived risk. It should resemble the customers you want to help's problem and make limitations clear.

checklist.label: Explain the before, approach and expected outcome
State ideas to test, limitations and required client inputs

warnings: Do not invent client results, testimonials or performance data.
steps.nextBestAction: Create one relevant proof asset and explain the outcome and limitations clearly.

steps.title: Make a Simple Work Page
steps.description: Present the customer, problem, offer and proof in one easy-to-review place.

content.text: A simple proof page helps likely customers decide whether to continue. It does not need to become a large brand project.

checklist.label: State who the service is for
Explain the problem and offered outcome
List scope boundaries and next step
Check that every claim is supportable

steps.nextBestAction: Publish one simple page or document that explains the offer and proof.

steps.title: Set a Trial Price and Clear Terms
steps.description: Choose initial terms using {{pricingFocus}}.

content.text: A paid trial should be small enough to reduce buyer risk but clear enough to test real delivery and costs and results.

checklist.label: Estimate delivery effort and direct expenses
Choose a fixed trial scope and price
Define payment, revisions and change requests
Define what happens after the trial

warnings: Do not use an unlimited-scope trial to win the first client.
steps.nextBestAction: Set one paid trial price with explicit scope, payment and revision boundaries.

steps.title: Talk to Likely Customers
steps.description: Contact {{outreachTarget}} likely customers through {{outreachChannel}}.

content.text: Responsible outreach should be relevant, specific and easy to decline. Quality of fit matters more than message volume.

checklist.label: Build a list of {{outreachTarget}} likely customers
Write a short message tied to an observable problem
Include the proof asset and a low-friction next step
Respect platform rules, privacy and opt-outs

warnings: Do not scrape restricted data or send deceptive, irrelevant or high-volume spam.
steps.nextBestAction: Send the focused offer to the next five likely customers and record responses.

steps.title: Book Your First Paying Client
steps.description: Turn a qualified conversation into {{firstPaidMilestone}} with written scope.

content.text: A real payment tests the problem, trust, offer and price together. Keep the clear action narrow enough to deliver well.

checklist.label: Document access, privacy or safety boundaries

decisionGates.question: Has a qualified customer agreed to {{firstPaidMilestone}} on clear terms?

options.label: Yes, prepare delivery
options.description: Move into the agreed trial and protect the scope.

options.label: Not yet
options.description: Review objections, qualification and outreach rather than offering unlimited free work.

steps.nextBestAction: Ask the strongest qualified prospect to approve the written paid trial.

steps.title: Deliver the Paid Trial
steps.description: Deliver {{pilotOutcome}} while controlling {{deliveryFocus}}.

content.text: The trial tests both customer value and your ability to deliver reliably. Record exceptions and effort instead of hiding them.

checklist.label: Confirm the baseline and success measure
Record effort, issues and the achieved outcome
Close access or hand over documentation safely

warnings: {{riskWarning}}
steps.nextBestAction: Deliver the next agreed trial milestone and record effort and outcome proof.

steps.title: Check the Result and Your Workload
steps.description: Compare the achieved outcome, customer feedback, effort and obvious costs and results.

content.text: A happy client is useful. But the offer also needs controlled scope and repeatable delivery. Improving or pausing is legitimate if either side is weak.

checklist.label: Compare the baseline with the achieved outcome
Ask the customer what created the most value
Review effort, revisions and direct expenses
List the delivery changes required before repeating

decisionGates.question: Can this outcome be delivered consistently on workable terms?

options.label: Yes, document and repeat
options.description: Collect proof and turn the strongest parts into a repeatable process.

options.label: Improve the offer
options.description: Return to scope and pricing before accepting another similar client.

options.label: Pause this offer
options.description: Record why value or delivery is weak and avoid selling the same promise again.

steps.nextBestAction: Review value, delivery effort and scope. then choose repeat, improve or pause.

steps.title: Ask for Feedback and a Referral
steps.description: Ask for honest proof only after the customer has experienced the outcome.

content.text: Specific proof and qualified referrals reduce future buyer risk. The customer should approve what can be shared.

checklist.label: Get permission for any testimonial or case detail
Request one relevant introduction if appropriate
Remove confidential details from public proof

steps.nextBestAction: Ask the customer for specific approved feedback and one relevant referral.

steps.title: Repeat What Works
steps.description: Turn the proof into {{scalePath}} without expanding beyond delivery capacity.

content.text: Standardization should improve consistency, qualification and handoff. It should not turn a custom service into an unrealistic one-size-fits-all promise.

checklist.label: Create a repeatable scope and delivery checklist
Update price or terms using trial proof
Choose one channel for the next qualified client

steps.nextBestAction: Document the repeatable offer and choose one controlled path to the next qualified client.

items.name: Online Business Start Plan
items.description: Follow one step at a time. Test the idea before you spend more.

variables.alternatives: existing tools, manual workarounds and switching barriers
variables.prototypeFormat: a mock-up, manual service or minimal interactive prototype
variables.acquisitionChannel: one channel where people you want to help already seek solutions
variables.operationsFocus: privacy, security, reliability, support and applicable disclosures
variables.retentionEvidence: repeat usage of the core plan and willingness to keep paying
variables.scalePath: one measured test to find users or improve the product
variables.riskWarning: Do not build a full product before the problem and core plan are tested.
variables.validationCriteria: confirm the recurring problem and take a clear next step

steps.title: Check If the Problem Is Real
steps.description: Confirm that {{user}} repeatedly experience {{problem}}.

content.text: A broad trend or search volume does not prove a useful product. Look for repeated behavior, consequences and a concrete clear action.

checklist.label: Interview at least {{validationTargetCount}} people you want to help
Document the current workaround and consequence
Ask for a trial, preorder, signup with intent or another clear next step

warnings: {{riskWarning}}

decisionGates.question: Did {{validationTargetCount}} people you want to help {{validationCriteria}}?

options.label: Yes, define the user
options.description: Write the people you want to help and use case before prototyping.

options.label: Not yet
options.description: Narrow the user or problem and test again before building.

steps.nextBestAction: Interview {{validationTargetCount}} people you want to help about the current workaround and ask for a concrete clear action.

steps.title: Pick One User and One Result
steps.description: Choose the user, trigger and core outcome for the first version.

content.text: A narrow product can solve one plan deeply enough to earn repeated use. Broad personas and feature lists hide weak demand.

checklist.label: Write the people you want to help and role
Define the trigger that starts the plan
State the input and desired outcome
List users and use cases the first version will not serve

steps.nextBestAction: Write one people you want to help, one trigger and one measurable plan outcome.

steps.title: See What Users Do Today
steps.description: Review {{alternatives}}.

content.text: The strongest competitor may be a spreadsheet, search habit or manual service. Understand why users tolerate it and what would justify switching.

checklist.label: Review at least five tools or workarounds
Record price, setup and switching effort
Write the unresolved gap your first version will test

steps.nextBestAction: Review five current alternatives and document the repeated unresolved gap.

steps.title: Build the Smallest Useful Demo
steps.description: Demonstrate the outcome with {{prototypeFormat}}.

content.text: A prototype tests flow and value before infrastructure. It can be partly manual as long as users experience the intended outcome honestly.

checklist.label: Observe people you want to help attempting the core outcome

warnings: {{riskWarning}}
steps.nextBestAction: Prototype the smallest end-to-end plan and observe people you want to help using it.

steps.title: Test One Way to Find Users
steps.description: Reach people you want to help through {{acquisitionChannel}}.

content.text: A product with no credible path to qualified users is not tested. Test one channel with a clear message before growing content or promotion.

checklist.label: Choose one qualified finding customers channel
Write a message around the observed problem and outcome
Put the prototype or offer in front of at least 20 relevant users
Record qualified visits, conversations and commitments

steps.nextBestAction: Reach 20 relevant users through one channel and record qualified actions, not impressions.

steps.title: Choose How You Get Paid
steps.description: Define {{revenueModel}} tied to the core outcome.

content.text: Pricing should test readiness to pay and acknowledge delivery or usage costs. Avoid complex tiers before the main value is understood.

checklist.label: Choose one paid offer or tier
Explain what the buyer receives and what is limited
Estimate obvious delivery or usage costs
Define cancellation, refund or disclosure expectations

steps.nextBestAction: Write one paid offer with value, limits and obvious delivery costs.

steps.title: Check Privacy, Support and Reliability
steps.description: Review {{operationsFocus}} before inviting broader use.

content.text: Online products can expose user data or create dependency. Keep data access minimal and explain limitations, support and fallback clearly.

checklist.label: Map user data and third-party dependencies
Check privacy, security and disclosure needs
Define support, reliability and human-fallback boundaries
Save current official guidance where requirements apply
Test failure and recovery for the core plan

warnings: Do not collect sensitive data or promise reliability you cannot support.
steps.nextBestAction: Map user data, dependencies and the fallback when the core plan fails.

steps.title: Launch the Smallest Useful Version
steps.description: Release the core plan to a small qualified user group.

content.text: A narrow release makes it possible to observe activation and support issues closely without hiding weak value behind traffic.

checklist.label: Release only the tested core plan
Observe the first successful and failed attempts
Respond to support and document repeated issues

steps.nextBestAction: Invite the first qualified cohort and observe whether each user reaches the core outcome.

steps.title: Get Your First Active Users
steps.description: Reach {{firstUserMilestone}} who complete the core plan.

content.text: Signups alone do not prove usefulness. Record activation, repeat behavior and why users stop.

checklist.label: Define the action that counts as activation
Ask inactive users where they became stuck
Track whether users return for the core plan

steps.nextBestAction: Help the next qualified user reach the core outcome and record whether they return.

steps.title: Get Your First Payment
steps.description: Work toward {{firstPaidMilestone}} without expanding the feature set.

content.text: Payment tests value, trust and pricing together. Early revenue matters only if users can receive the promised outcome and support remains manageable.

checklist.label: Ask activated users to accept the paid offer
Record each payment and finding customers source
Ask why buyers paid and why others declined

decisionGates.question: Have you reached {{firstPaidMilestone}} using the core plan?

options.label: Yes, review people coming back
options.description: Review repeat usage, support and willingness to continue paying.

options.label: Not yet
options.description: Return to the finding customers, core value or paid offer before adding features.

steps.nextBestAction: Ask the strongest activated user to accept the paid offer and record the decision.

steps.title: Review Use, Income and Risk
steps.description: Decide using {{retentionEvidence}}, support burden and obvious costs and results.

content.text: A launch spike is not a durable business. growing is justified only when the core plan is useful repeatedly and the paid model remains workable.

checklist.label: Review payment, cancellations and support effort
Review usage or delivery costs and dependencies
Write the strongest continue and stop proof

decisionGates.question: Does the proof support another measured investment?

options.label: Grow by Repeating What Works
options.description: Choose one finding customers or product experiment with a stop condition.

options.label: Improve the core value
options.description: Return to the prototype and fix the largest barrier to repeat use.

options.label: Pause this idea
options.description: Record why repeat use or paid value is weak and avoid adding more features.

steps.nextBestAction: Review repeat usage, payment and support proof and choose grow, improve or pause.

steps.title: Grow What Is Working
steps.description: Run {{scalePath}} after {{finalDecisionMilestone}}.

content.text: Choose one bottleneck supported by proof. More features, traffic and infrastructure at once make it impossible to learn what changed.

checklist.label: Choose one finding customers, activation or people coming back experiment
Define the user and expected behavior
Set a time, cost and stop limit
Protect privacy, reliability and support boundaries

steps.nextBestAction: Write one measured experiment with a user behavior target, budget and stop condition.

items.name: {{businessName}} Start Plan
items.description: A dedicated guided journey for {{businessName}}: small tests first, real proof later.

steps.title: Pick One Buyer
steps.description: Choose one clear buyer or occasion. Write one sentence: "I want to sell ___ to ___."

content.text: Choose one clear buyer or occasion. Write one sentence: "I want to sell ___ to ___."

checklist.label: Who exactly will buy your candles?

steps.nextBestAction: Pick one occasion. Choose one clear buyer or occasion. Write one sentence: "I want to sell ___ to ___."

steps.title: See What Already Sells
steps.description: Check 5–10 candle listings and local sellers. Note sizes, scents, prices, packaging and repeated complaints.

content.text: Check 5–10 candle listings and local sellers. Note sizes, scents, prices, packaging and repeated complaints.

checklist.label: Check 5–10 candles buyers can already choose
Write down the price range you saw

steps.nextBestAction: Check 5–10 candles buyers can already choose.

steps.title: Choose Your Tiny Range
steps.description: Pick only 2–3 candle variants for the first test. Avoid many scents and sizes.
